messages:
Sam (CS): Heads up — Acme (Marco) is seeing a flood of 429s when their CI spins up ~150 runners for init. Happens immediately during the warmup. Can we triage? :wave:
Priya (Eng): Marco, which SDK/version and can you paste any x-rate-limit headers and how you call init?
Marco (Customer): js-sdk v2.1.0. Header snippet:
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
x-rate-limit-limit: 60
x-rate-limit-remaining: 0
x-rate-limit-reset: 45
We do `workers.map(w => sdk.init({key: ENV.KEY}))` — all parallel.
Olivia (SRE): Classic preflight fanout + connection churn. Each worker doing a fresh handshake will exhaust the token/conn budget.
Priya (Eng): Two quick fixes: 1) add jitter and cap concurrent inits, 2) enable HTTP keep-alive / connection reuse. Example: use p-map with concurrency 6 and small random sleep before init.
Sam (CS): Also recommend Node agent: `new https.Agent({keepAlive:true, maxSockets:50})` to reduce TLS handshakes.
Olivia (SRE): We can temporarily increase Acme's rate bucket for onboarding CI runs while they implement the client change.
onboard-bot: Ticket CS-1029 opened; temp rate bump requested for org-acme.
Marco (Customer): Implemented jitter+concurrency=6 and keepAlive. Re-ran CI — no 429s now. Thanks! :tada:
Priya (Eng): We'll add a short cookbook note to onboarding docs about staggering SDK init and reusing connections for CI warmups.
Sam (CS): I'll record this in Acme's account health and mark renewal risk as mitigated.
Olivia (SRE): I'll relax the alert sensitivity (1m window) to avoid noisy flaps during rolling warmups. If Acme needs larger capacity routinely, Sales can coordinate a trial for Dedicated.
Marco (Customer): Confirmed stable. Appreciate the quick response.
Sam (CS): Closing loop — follow up in the enablement checklist.
